diagnostic_evidence.quote: The result directly follows from the Sokhotski-Plemelj formula

issues.failure_explanation: The tangent factor in the complex line element dξ is essential both for recovering the normal derivative kernel as a real part and for applying the Sokhotski–Plemelj formula. The definition instead uses |dξ|, while the proof silently switches to dξ. With the stated definition, Re f_D need not equal the real double-layer potential and the asserted jump formula does not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the arc-length element by the correctly oriented complex line element in the analytic Cauchy-type term and check the resulting orientation and jump signs throughout the definition and proof.
issues.overall_effect: The complex-potential lemma is false as defined, and the proofs of the double-layer nullspace description, the characteristic-operator injectivity, and the multiply connected Dirichlet formulation lose their stated support.
issues.title: Complex double-layer potential uses arc length instead of the complex line element
issues.why_classification: The proof already uses the intended complex line element, so a short local correction and sign check preserves the substantive results without new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Since z−conjugate(z)=2i Im(z), its square is −4 Im(z)^2, not +4 Im(z)^2. Thus the displayed f_G has real part −(1/(2π))log|theta_1(z)|−Im(z)^2/(2b), with the opposite sign from G.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the quadratic term to −(z−conjugate(z))^2/(8b) and correct the associated calculation.
issues.overall_effect: Part (3) of the complex-layer lemma is false as written.
issues.title: Incorrect sign in the proposed complex representation of the Green function
issues.why_classification: A local sign correction fully restores this isolated identity and does not alter subsequent results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \(\mathcal{S}\colon C(\partial \Omega) \to C(\partial \Omega) \) is a compact linear operator.
Furthermore, by Theorem~\ref{thm: neumann}, $\mathcal{S}[\psi]+ C$ solves Neumann BVP~\eqref{eqn: neumann} with boundary data $g$, for any $C\in \mathbb{R}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes a continuous boundary trace obtained from Sψ, but the paper proves only S:C→C and supplies no argument that arbitrary continuous Neumann data yield a continuously differentiable boundary trace. The asserted codomain C_0^1 is therefore stronger than the demonstrated mapping property.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a valid complex-valued periodic parametrization for each centered trefoil and rerun the affected numerical experiment and convergence comparison.
issues.overall_effect: The trefoil domains in Example 2 are not defined by the stated construction, so the associated error, convergence-rate, and comparison claims cannot be reproduced from the source.
issues.title: Trefoil parametrization does not define a planar boundary curve
issues.why_classification: Repair requires reconstructing the actual domains and recomputing the numerical evidence, but not changing the global layer-potential method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To generate the holes, we randomly chose each center \( a_i, i \in [M] \), an oscillation factor \( \omega_i \in [3,7] \), and the maximum radius of the hole \( r_i \).
The boundary of each hole \(\partial D_i \) is parametrized by~\eqref{eqn: neumann bdry shape}.

issues.failure_explanation: The map is real-valued and omits both the center a_i and the complex unit direction needed to produce a closed planar boundary. Consequently it does not define the claimed holes and does not make r_i their stated maximum radius.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide the intended complex-valued centered boundary parametrization, verify disjointness of the resulting holes, and rerun Examples 3 and 6.
issues.overall_effect: The geometries used in Neumann Example 3 and Steklov Example 6 are not specified by the source, undermining reproducibility of their numerical values and plots.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The eigenpairs $(\sigma, \vec{\phi})$ are computed using MATLAB's built-in function \texttt{eig}.
We estimate that the error in $\sigma_k$ are on the order of $10^{-14}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The reported residual is evaluated at the same grid points where the discrete generalized eigenproblem enforces the boundary equation, so a machine-precision residual primarily measures the algebraic eigensolve. The source gives no independent continuous residual evaluation or discretization-error estimate connecting this collocation residual to the exact Steklov spectrum.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Evaluate the boundary residual independently at sufficiently many non-collocation points and supply the hypotheses and constants needed for a valid spectral inclusion or eigenvalue-error bound.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed approximately 10^−14 relative accuracy for the 25-hole Steklov eigenvalues is not established by the reported data.
issues.title: Collocation residual is treated as a posteriori eigenvalue-error evidence

issues.failure_explanation: Transposition moves a source quadrature weight h_j into a target-index position, whereas Nyström discretization of D* still requires the source weight. Thus D_s=D^T only in special equal-weight cases. In general the discrete adjoint relation is weighted, of the form D_s=W^{-1}D^T W, rather than an ordinary transpose.

failure_location.quote: Note that \( D_s = D^T \), where $D$ is defined in Appendix~\ref{s: dirichlet num implementation}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Construct D_s directly with source weights, or use the correct weighted-transpose relation, and rerun affected Neumann and Steklov computations.
issues.overall_effect: Any implementation constructing D_s by ordinary transposition gives the wrong Neumann and Steklov matrices on nonuniform-speed or unequal-weight boundaries, including the stated irregular-hole examples.
issues.title: Weighted Nyström adjoint matrix is not the ordinary transpose
issues.why_classification: The matrix construction has a standard contained repair, but affected numerical experiments and guarantees require recomputation.

issues.failure_explanation: The product-integration coefficients R_j already contain the quadrature scaling for integration in t. For the arc-length integral they should multiply the sampled density times |z'(t_j)|, not h_j=w_j|z'(t_j)|. Multiplying by h_j introduces an additional ordinary quadrature weight and scales the singular part incorrectly.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace h_j R_j by |z'(t_j)|R_j in the singular product-integration block, verify normalization conventions, and recompute all Steklov examples.
issues.overall_effect: The matrix claimed to discretize the single-layer operator is incorrect, invalidating the stated Steklov discretization and its numerical eigenvalues as generated by the written algorithm.
issues.title: Singular quadrature weights are multiplied twice
issues.why_classification: The quadrature formula can be repaired locally, but the full set of Steklov numerical results must be regenerated.

issues.failure_explanation: The matrix for S_0 must include the additive mean term: discretely it is S(I−M)+M, not S(I−M). The written pencil annihilates every constant vector on both sides, making it a singular 0/0 direction and failing to represent the zero Steklov eigenpair. It also is not the discretization of the formal boundary integral equation.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the right-hand matrix S(I−M)+M, handle the zero mode explicitly if necessary, and rerun and independently validate all Steklov computations.
